extra.message: The user-controlled query parameter 'fragment' is string-concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template source ('Result: ' + fragment) before compilation, then rendered. An attacker can submit Jinja2 syntax (e.g. {{ ''.__class__...__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}) to achieve server-side template injection and remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: User-controlled query parameter 'host' is concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to os.system(). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; cat /etc/passwd') to execute arbitrary commands.

cwe: CWE-78: OS Command Injection

extra.message: pickle.loads() is called on the raw request body (or a query-string 'blob', optionally base64-decoded) supplied by the client. Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted payload.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: lxml.etree.XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True and resolve_entities=True (and no_network=False) while parsing the raw client-supplied request body. This allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks to read local files or trigger SSRF via external/parameter entities.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The client-supplied JSON body ('filter' or the entire payload) is passed unvalidated as the query document to MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g. {"$where": ...} or {"$ne": null}) to bypass intended filtering or exfiltrate data.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: eval() is called on the user-controlled query parameter 'expr'. Although __builtins__ is restricted, eval() with attacker-controlled expressions is a well-known sandbox-escape vector (e.g. via object introspection through the provided locals) enabling code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)

extra.message: The client-supplied 'name' parameter is joined directly onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR and written with the raw request body, without sanitizing path separators or '..' sequences. An attacker can supply a path like '../../etc/cron.d/x' to write files outside the intended export directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: The client-supplied 'ref' value (query param or JSON body) is used unsanitized to build the export filename f'{ref}.json' under BASE_EXPORT_DIR. A value containing '../' allows writing outside the export directory (path traversal).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: SSN and full card number values taken directly from the client-supplied JSON payload are written in cleartext to a JSON file on disk with no encryption or masking, exposing sensitive PII/PCI data to anyone with filesystem access.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: An outbound HTTPS request to a partner endpoint is made using ssl._create_unverified_context(), disabling certificate verification and hostname checking. This allows man-in-the-middle interception/spoofing of the partner response.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: The user-controlled query parameter 'card' is rendered into an HTML response through a Jinja2 template using the '|safe' filter, which disables autoescaping. An attacker can supply HTML/JS (e.g. '<script>...</script>') that executes in the victim's browser (reflected XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-Site Scripting)

extra.message: The user-controlled 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse without validating that it points to a same-origin/allow-listed destination, enabling attackers to craft links that redirect victims to arbitrary external sites (phishing).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: The Origin request header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This permits any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response, defeating same-origin protections.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The exception message interpolates the client-supplied 'lot_ref' and the internal BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path, and the full exception string plus exception class name are returned directly in the HTTP response body, leaking internal path/implementation details to callers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The raw Authorization header value and full request body are written to the application log at WARNING level. Logged credentials/secrets can be exposed to anyone with log access or via log-aggregation pipelines.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The endpoint recomputes an in-memory 'ledger' balance directly from a client-supplied 'amount' and lets the client also set the resulting 'state' field (default 'approved') with no server-side validation of the transaction, allowing a caller to force an arbitrary balance/approval outcome.

cwe: CWE-840: Business Logic Errors

extra.message: The response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and an empty Content-Security-Policy, disabling browser-side XSS mitigations and framing/script-source restrictions for this endpoint.

cwe: CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: The internal ops gate token is compared with '!=' (a short-circuiting, non-constant-time comparison) instead of a constant-time function such as security.constant_time_equal (already used elsewhere in this codebase for CSRF tokens). This can allow a timing side-channel to recover the token.

cwe: CWE-208: Observable Timing Discrepancy

extra.message: Handle-to-verifier mappings ('north'->'4812', 'south'->'5930') are hardcoded in source, and the verifier check uses a plain '!=' comparison instead of a constant-time compare, allowing both credential disclosure via source access and timing-based brute force.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The 'count' query parameter has no upper bound validation and directly controls the size of a list built in memory (range(count)). A large value can exhaust memory/CPU on the server.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The endpoint returns the internal APP_ENV value and the resolved BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path in the response body, exposing internal deployment details.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The raw password-reset token and the user's email are appended in cleartext to a local log file (local_mocks/password_resets.log) unconditionally on every reset request, regardless of environment. Anyone with read access to this file can hijack any pending password reset.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The session cookie set after self-registration hardcodes secure=False, unlike the /api/auth/login handler which honors the COOKIE_SECURE environment variable (line 428). In a production deployment with COOKIE_SECURE=true, newly registered users still receive a session cookie without the Secure flag, allowing it to be sent over plain HTTP.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: A hardcoded demo password 'DemoPass123!' is used to create every seeded account (admin, dispatcher, workers, customers), and a hardcoded API key 'fd_demo_status_key_please_rotate' (line 309) and webhook secret 'local-demo-secret' (line 304) are seeded into the database. If this seed script is ever run against a shared or production-reachable database, these become known, guessable credentials.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The default DATABASE_URL falls back to a hardcoded credential pair (dispatch:dispatch) when the environment variable is unset, which can silently connect to a database with a well-known default password if misconfigured in deployment.
